_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Vietnam covering Ông Bích/Dong Son bronze drums, Chinese domination 111 BCE-939 CE, Trưng Sisters rebellion, Ly/Tran/Le dynasties, Mongol invasions repelled, Champa conflicts, Tây Sơn rebellion, Nguyễn Dynasty, French colonization (Indochina 1887-1954), WWII Japanese occupation, Hồ Chí Minh's independence 1945, First Indochina War 1946-54 (Diện Biên Phủ), partition, Vietnam War 1955-1975 (3M+ dead), Fall of Saigon 1975, reunification, Đổi Mới reforms 1986, and recent economic growth under CPV.

religion.note: Ancestor worship/folk religion dominant; Mahayana Buddhism; Confucian/Taoist syncretism; Catholic legacy (8%; Diệm and Ngô family Catholic); Cao Dai (syncretic, Tay Ninh); Hoa Hao (Buddhist reform, Mekong); CPV officially atheist but tolerates religion

ethnic_groups.name: Kinh (Viet)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnic Vietnamese; Austroasiatic; Red River/Mekong deltas; politically dominant; Han Chinese cultural influence (Confucian, sinographic script historically); Vietnam War 'Vietnamese'; CPV

ethnic_groups.name: Tay
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern highlands; Tai-Kadai; second-largest minority; rice terraces; cross-border with China

ethnic_groups.name: Thai
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwest; Tai-Kadai; Black Thai, White Thai subgroups; distinct from Thailand Thais

ethnic_groups.name: Muong
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern mountains; Austroasiatic; linguistically close to Kinh; Hoa Binh area

ethnic_groups.name: Khmer Krom
ethnic_groups.notes: Mekong Delta; ethnic Khmer; Theravada Buddhist; ~1.3M; annexed from Cambodia (Cochinchina); Cambodian grievance; some discrimination

ethnic_groups.name: Hmong (Mong)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern highlands; Hmong-Mien; fought with French/US (some); Sapa; opium historically; cross-border

ethnic_groups.name: Hoa (Chinese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnic Chinese; Cantonese/Teochew; Saigon/Cholon (Chinatown); merchants; many fled 1978-79 (boat people, anti-Chinese campaign); now ~1M

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Dao, Gia Rai, Ede, Ba Na, Cham, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: 53 officially recognized ethnic groups; Dao (Yao); Gia Rai/Ede (Central Highlands, Austronesian, Montagnard, US allies Vietnam War); Cham (Muslim/Hindu, remnant of Champa kingdom); diverse hill tribes

independence.date: 1945-09-02 (declared from Japan), 1954-07-21 (recognized after First Indochina War), 1975-04-30 (reunification)
independence.from: France (1954), reunified after defeating South Vietnam/US (1975)

country_profile.notes_unique: Vietnam War (American War, 1955-75, ~3M dead including 58,000 US); Fall of Saigon April 30, 1975 (iconic helicopter); Hồ Chí Minh (Uncle Ho, independence icon); Diện Biên Phủ 1954 (French defeated); boat people (1978-80s refugees); Agent Orange (dioxin, birth defects); Cu Chi tunnels; My Lai massacre; Đổi Mới 1986 (economic reforms, market socialism); one-party CPV rule; Hanoi vs Saigon (HCMC) divide; pho, bánh mì; South China Sea disputes (Spratly/Paracel)

natural_resources.notes: Significant rare earth reserves (world's 2nd largest deposits); coal production declining as consumption rises; bauxite development controversial (Central Highlands).

military.notes: Large standing army; 'Four No's' defense policy; modernizing with Russian/Israeli equipment; South China Sea fleet expansion; Cam Ranh Bay strategic naval base; veteran force from decades of conflict.

infrastructure.notes: North-South Expressway under construction; Reunification Express railway (Hanoi-HCMC 30 hours); ambitious metro systems (Hanoi/HCMC) delayed; extensive waterway network in Mekong Delta.

climate_environment.notes: Climate change top-5 most vulnerable country; Mekong Delta sinking/saltwater intrusion; Agent Orange contamination legacy; new species still discovered regularly; reforestation success story.

debt_aid.notes: Graduated from IDA 2017; ODA declining as income rises; JICA largest bilateral donor; conservative fiscal management; public debt under 40% GDP ceiling.

top_universities: Hanoi University of Science and Technology
education.notes: PISA scores remarkably high for income level (outperform many OECD countries); strong STEM focus; rote learning criticized; growing international education sector.

diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Labor export program (Japan/Korea/Taiwan); attracting overseas Vietnamese (Viet Kieu)
diaspora_migration.notes: Viet Kieu diaspora (especially USA ~2M) economically significant; labor migrants to Japan/Korea rapidly increasing; $19B remittances among world's top 10.

digital_economy.notes: FPT Corporation leading tech conglomerate; VNG unicorn; mobile-first economy; government push for digital transformation; gaming industry significant.

country_profile.national_motto: Doc Lap, Tu Do, Hanh Phuc (Independence, Freedom, Happiness)
country_profile.national_anthem: Tien Quan Ca (The Song of the Marching Troops)

geography.terrain: S-shaped; Red River Delta north; Mekong Delta south; Central Highlands; Annamite Range along western border
geography.notes: S-shaped country stretching 1,650 km north-south; only 50 km wide at narrowest; Mekong Delta produces half of rice; South China Sea territorial disputes.

economy_extended.notes: One of world's fastest-growing economies; Doi Moi reforms (1986) transformed from central planning to market socialism; Samsung's largest global production base; major FDI destination shifting from China; CPTPP member.

health.notes: Impressive health outcomes for income level; universal health insurance (90%+ coverage); high out-of-pocket costs; Agent Orange legacy (birth defects/cancer); COVID zero strategy initially successful.

food_agriculture.notes: World's 2nd/3rd largest rice exporter; largest robusta coffee producer; top cashew, pepper, and pangasius exporter; Mekong Delta threatened by sea-level rise and upstream dams.

energy.notes: Rooftop solar boom (2020-2021); rapidly growing energy demand; coal imports increasing; Power Development Plan 8 (PDP8) targets 30% renewables by 2030; offshore wind potential enormous (160GW).

major_airports_international: Tan Son Nhat (Ho Chi Minh City)
major_seaports: Ho Chi Minh City (Cat Lai/Hiep Phuoc)
transport.notes: Long Thanh Airport (HCMC) mega-project under construction (~$16B); motorbike-dominated traffic (45M+ motorbikes); Hai Phong deep-water port; Vietjet Air rapid growth.

unesco_sites_list: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
tourism.notes: Pre-COVID target 18M visitors; recovering strongly; e-visa program expanded; backpacker/cultural tourism destination; street food culture globally famous.

human_rights_gender.notes: One-party communist state; no opposition parties permitted; high women's workforce participation; online censorship extensive; 2024 anti-corruption campaign ('blazing furnace') sweeping.

border_disputes: South China Sea (Paracel/Spratly Islands vs China)
security_stability.notes: Stable internally; South China Sea is major security concern; modernizing naval/air capabilities; balancing China-US relations ('bamboo diplomacy').

legal_system.notes: Communist Party leadership enshrined; land owned by state (use rights only); 2013 Constitution modernized; commercial courts improving; anti-corruption courts established.

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Growing domestic market; Vietnamese-American diaspora filmmakers
intangible_heritage_items: Quan ho Bac Ninh folk songs (UNESCO ICH)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: State-controlled; online censorship via Cybersecurity Law 2018; Vietnamese-language internet vibrant
cultural_heritage.notes: Pho and banh mi globally iconic; water puppetry unique art form; 4 UNESCO intangible heritage items; ao dai national dress; coffee culture (largest robusta producer).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Rankings within Southeast Asia (11 countries). 3rd most populous in SE Asia; fastest growing major economy.

current_leader.notes: Public Security background; anti-corruption czar; consolidated power; holds both top posts (unusual); conservative; CPV collective leadership model

former_leaders.name: Trường Chinh
former_leaders.notes: Ideologue; land reform disaster 1950s (~10,000 killed); briefly General Secretary

former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; Vietnam War leader; hardliner; southern guerrilla commander; reunification architect; died 1986

former_leaders.notes: General (not head of state); Diện Biên Phủ victor; military genius; Defense Minister; 'Red Napoleon'; Tết Offensive; died 2013; national hero
